clue.text: Salt I love to put on fruit

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring, the letter O
a date is the fruit of the date palm

explanation.surface: Someone declares they enjoy sprinkling salt on their fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to put on' simply joins the pieces in order: I, then O, then DATE.
explanation.definitionFit: An iodate is a chemical salt of iodic acid, such as potassium iodate added to table salt.

clue.text: Like our boss, wanting slave ultimately for excessive exploitation

parts.note: our boss is placed over us

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word slave

explanation.surface: A tyrannical boss who wants a slave is guilty of exploitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like our boss' is read as OVER US; 'ultimately' supplies the E ending slave.
explanation.definitionFit: Overuse is using something too much, and excessive exploitation means much the same.

clue.text: Former lady in Parliament? Bright star, but no leader

indicators.note: no leader means the first letter of the star's name is cut off

parts.note: Castor is one of the two brightest stars in Gemini

explanation.surface: A former female MP was a shining star, though never the party leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but no leader' removes C from CASTOR. Nancy Astor was the first woman to take a seat in the British House of Commons, in 1919.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Astor was the first female member to sit in the House of Commons, so she is a former lady in Parliament.

clue.text: Rash guy from Austin maybe heading off with the old woman

indicators.note: heading off means the guy's initial letter is removed

parts.note: Austin is the capital of Texas, so a man from there is a Texan
ma is an informal word for mother, the old woman

explanation.surface: An impulsive Texan sets off with his mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rash' looks like an adjective for the guy, but it is a skin eruption. 'heading off' takes T from TEXAN, leaving EXAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An exanthema is a skin eruption accompanying a disease such as measles, a medical term for a rash.

clue.text: Hang about after accident — not good sort of road

indicators.note: after an accident things are smashed up, so the letters are thrown into a new order
not means the letter for good is dropped from the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone is told to wait around at the scene of a crash on a dangerous road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes G from HANGABOUT, leaving HANABOUT; 'after accident' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An autobahn is a German motorway, a particular type of high-speed road.

clue.text: A doctor on revolutionary course about certain glands

indicators.note: revolutionary means the word for course is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: a lane is a course, as in a running track or swimming pool

explanation.surface: A doctor on a radical training course learns about some glands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' signals the reversal of the course word. The definition is adjectival: 'about certain glands' means relating to them.
explanation.definitionFit: Adrenal is an adjective meaning relating to the adrenal glands, which sit on the kidneys.

clue.text: Travels made by band beginning to end

indicators.note: the starting letter of the word for band is moved to its end

parts.note: a strip is a narrow band

explanation.surface: A rock group's tours run from start to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' suggests musicians, but it is a strip of material; 'beginning to end' sends its S to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Trips are journeys, so the plural noun matches travels in the sense of journeys made.

clue.text: Fashionable society? Spooner's cut connection

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of word pairs, so the pair's first consonants change places

parts.note: to mow is to cut grass
a bond is a connection

explanation.surface: A query about whether a Spoonerism severed ties with high society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spooner's' swaps the initial sounds of MOW BOND to give 'bow mond', heard as the French phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Beau monde is French for 'beautiful world', used in English for the fashionable elite.

clue.text: Spirited lasses left out of religious retreats

indicators.note: out of means the letter for left is taken out of the phrase for religious retreats

parts.note: holy means religious or sacred
dens are private retreats or hideaways

explanation.surface: Lively young women have been excluded from religious retreats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes L from HOLY DENS.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoyden is a boisterous, high-spirited girl, so the plural means spirited lasses.

clue.text: Surprising additional charge for coat?

parts.note: something additional is extra
in heraldry an ordinary is one of the simple geometric charges placed on a coat of arms

explanation.surface: A shopper is startled to be billed an extra fee just for their coat.
explanation.walkthrough: The coat is a coat of arms and the charge is a heraldic device, not a fee: an ordinary is a basic heraldic charge such as a bend or chevron.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extraordinary is remarkable or unexpected, a straightforward synonym for surprising.

clue.text: Class being terminated early after month, making one browned off

indicators.note: after places the class piece behind the month in the answer

parts.note: Aug is the abbreviation for August

indicators.note: stopped before its end, so the final letter of the word for class is lost

parts.note: a rating is a class or grade

explanation.surface: A course is cancelled a month in, leaving someone fed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'browned off' looks like British slang for annoyed, but here it is literal: a dish browned on top.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish served au gratin has a crust of breadcrumbs or cheese browned under the grill.

clue.text: Cake with lemon is somehow nothing to be missed

indicators.note: somehow says the remaining letters are put together in some other way
to be missed means the letter for nothing is left out of the fodder

parts.note: nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A lemon cake is somehow so good it must not be missed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be missed' drops O from LEMONIS, leaving LEMNIS, for the anagram indicator to rearrange. A simnel cake is a British fruit cake with marzipan, eaten at Easter.
explanation.definitionFit: Simnel cake is a traditional British Easter fruitcake topped with marzipan balls.

clue.text: French department store's customer?

definitions.meaning: the Vendée is a department of western France
the person to whom something is sold, a buyer

explanation.surface: A shopper in a French department store.
explanation.definitionFit: Vendée names a French administrative region, and a vendee in legal usage is the purchaser in a sale.

clue.text: Male meeting female — it comes after party, bringing distress

indicators.note: comes after places the male, female and it pieces behind the party in the answer

parts.note: a disco is a dancing party

explanation.surface: A man and woman meet, and what follows a party leaves them upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bringing' is a link to the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To discomfit is to make someone uneasy or embarrassed, so it works as a verb synonym of distress.

clue.text: Classics teacher maybe has to turn around one idiot coming in bottom of the class?

indicators.note: coming in means the turned piece goes inside the word for bottom of the class

parts.note: the pupil at the bottom of the class comes last

indicators.note: turning around means the letters for one and idiot are read backwards

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a nit is a fool, an idiot

explanation.surface: A teacher of Latin has to deal with a dim pupil languishing at the foot of the class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn around' reverses one plus idiot, giving TINI, and 'coming in' sets that inside the word for bottom of the class.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latinist is a scholar of Latin, and a classics teacher is one example of such a person.

clue.text: Various teashops around university? They offer something stronger than tea

definitions.text: They offer something stronger than tea

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters surround the letter for university
various suggests a different arrangement of the letters of teashops

explanation.surface: A tour of the many tea rooms around a university town, versus the pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Various' rearranges TEASHOPS, which 'around' wraps about U.
explanation.definitionFit: A taphouse is a tavern serving beer on draught, offering a drink stronger than tea.

clue.text: Provision for boater after journey home?

definitions.text: Provision for boater after journey home?

parts.words: Provision for boater after journey home?
parts.note: a boater is a flat straw hat, not a person in a boat; on arriving home you hang it up on a piece of hall furniture

explanation.surface: Someone who has travelled by boat needs something waiting for them at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boater' suggests a sailor, but it is the stiff straw hat, which needs somewhere to go once you are indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatstand is a pole with hooks for hanging hats and coats, so it provides a place for a straw hat.

clue.text: New manual on etiquette originally provided for former students

indicators.note: new means the letters of manual are made into a fresh word
originally picks the first letter of etiquette

explanation.surface: A new etiquette manual is issued to past pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges MANUAL; 'originally' gives E from etiquette.
explanation.definitionFit: Alumnae are female graduates or former pupils of a school or college.

clue.text: Daughter is left to play about

parts.note: port is the left-hand side of a ship

explanation.surface: A daughter is left alone to amuse herself.
explanation.walkthrough: PORT is the nautical term for left.
explanation.definitionFit: To disport is to frolic or amuse oneself, an old-fashioned word for playing about.

clue.text: Intertwine branches of fruit tree across short line

indicators.note: the fruit tree is placed across, spanning, the letter for line, so that letter sits inside

parts.note: a peach is a fruit tree
L is the short form of line

explanation.surface: A gardener weaves the branches of a fruit tree across a line of wire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' makes PEACH straddle L.
explanation.definitionFit: To pleach is to interlace the branches of trees or hedges to form a screen or arbour.

clue.text: Fellow losing head interrupting players before start of Ashes game

indicators.note: before puts the players piece ahead of the start of Ashes
interrupting means the shortened fellow breaks into the word for players

parts.note: the cast of a play are its players

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter of the word for fellow is dropped

parts.note: a fellow is a man

indicators.note: start of picks the first letter of Ashes

explanation.surface: A cricketer is hit on the head while at the crease before the Ashes series starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' beheads the fellow and 'interrupting' puts what remains among the players. The Ashes is the England–Australia cricket series.
explanation.definitionFit: Canasta is a card game in the rummy family, played with two packs.

clue.text: Fortification brought to light by archaeologist?

definitions.meaning: a trench shelter, a defensive earthwork
an archaeologist's finds are literally ... of the ground

explanation.surface: An ancient fort is excavated by an archaeologist.
explanation.definitionFit: A dugout is a roofed military trench, and anything excavated from the earth has been unearthed by digging.

clue.text: Group in fiery furnace, say, featuring in article about religious lessons

indicators.note: about means the definite article is wrapped round the letters for religious lessons

parts.note: the is the definite article
RE is religious education, a school subject

explanation.surface: A newspaper article about scripture lessons mentions the group in the fiery furnace.
explanation.walkthrough: Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego, three men in the Book of Daniel, were thrown into a fiery furnace; 'about' wraps the article round the school subject.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical trio in the furnace are an example of a group numbering three.

clue.text: Confess, having received unfriendly rebuke

indicators.note: having received means the word for confess takes in the other piece

parts.note: to sing is slang for confessing to the police
a cold manner is unfriendly

explanation.surface: Someone owns up and is given a frosty telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having received' signals the container; to sing is criminal slang for informing or confessing.
explanation.definitionFit: A scolding is an angry reprimand, so it serves as a synonym for a rebuke as a noun.

clue.text: Fantasy of fear doubled at the end

indicators.note: the closing letter, a Roman numeral, is doubled in value: 500 becomes 1000

parts.note: dread is fear

explanation.surface: A fantasy where a fear grows twice as great in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: D is Roman 500; doubled it is 1000, M, so 'doubled at the end' swaps DREAD's last D for M.
explanation.definitionFit: A dream is an imagined scenario or wish, a synonym for fantasy.

clue.text: Villainy of Russian seen all over the place

indicators.note: scattered all over the place means the letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A Russian villain's wickedness is seen everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over the place' rearranges the thirteen letters of OF RUSSIAN SEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Nefariousness is wickedness or criminality, a direct synonym for villainy.

clue.text: Conscious of emotion when maiden has departed

indicators.note: departed means the letter for maiden leaves the word for emotion

parts.note: sentiment is a feeling or emotion
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Someone is aware of their feelings once a young woman has left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has departed' removes M from SENTIMENT; a maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentient being can perceive and feel, so the word is a synonym for being aware.

clue.text: See deer dance by river

parts.note: the samba is a Brazilian dance
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: An invitation to watch a deer dancing beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is only a link; the definition is 'deer', with SAMBA followed by R.
explanation.definitionFit: The sambar is a large South Asian deer with rugged antlers.
